## The Data

```{r data}
study_time <- c(12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 22, 25, 27, 28, 30,
                 30, 31, 33, 35, 36, 38, 40, 42, 45, 50)
study_time
```

---

## 8.

### (a) Frequency Table

```{r freq-table}
breaks <- seq(10, 54, by = 5)
bins <- cut(study_time, breaks = breaks, right = FALSE)
freq_table <- table(bins)
freq_table
```

### (b) Histogram

```{r histogram}
hist(study_time,
     breaks = breaks,
     right = FALSE,
     col = "lightblue",
     border = "black",
     main = "Histogram of Study Time",
     xlab = "Study Time (minutes)",
     ylab = "Frequency")
```

### (c) Shape of the Distribution

The distribution is close to symmetric, but it slightly skews right. 

---

## 9. Box Plot 

### (a) Five Number Summary

```{r five-number-summary}
summary(study_time)
```

```{r quartiles}
Q1 <- quantile(study_time, 0.25)
Q3 <- quantile(study_time, 0.75)
med <- median(study_time)
min_val <- min(study_time)
max_val <- max(study_time)

c(Min = min_val, Q1 = Q1, Median = med, Q3 = Q3, Max = max_val)
```

### (b) IQR and Outlier Check

```{r iqr-outliers}
IQR_val <- Q3 - Q1
lower_fence <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_val
upper_fence <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val

IQR_val
lower_fence
upper_fence

# Any values outside the fences are outliers
outliers <- study_time[study_time < lower_fence | study_time > upper_fence]
outliers
```
numeric(0) means no outliers

### (c) Box Plot

```{r boxplot}
boxplot(study_time,
        horizontal = TRUE,
        col = "lightgreen",
        main = "Box Plot of Study Time",
        xlab = "Study Time (minutes)")
```

---

## 10. Comparison

**(a) Mean vs. Median**

```{r mean-median}
mean(study_time)
median(study_time)
```

I would say the median is the best measure of the center. The histogram showed a large amount of instances between 30 and 35. The median came out to exactly 30.
